=== DOCS-TRUTH RE-PINNED (verified against trino.io/docs/467 mental model) ===
• Pattern D rolling-avg-of-daily-X — Trino 467: 'N-day moving average of DAILY <metric>' requires the window operand to be ALREADY one-row-per-day. For raw per-event/per-order source: pre-aggregate to one row per day FIRST in a CTE with `SUM(metric) GROUP BY date`, THEN window the daily series with `AVG(daily_metric) OVER (ORDER BY date ROWS BETWEEN N-1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)`. The DO-NOT-WRITE is `AVG(amount) OVER (ORDER BY order_date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)` directly on `orders` — that averages individual per-order amounts over ~6 ORDERS back (a sliver of a single day), not 7 daily totals. Two-things-wrong: (1) frame counts rows not days, (2) avg is over per-order not per-day amounts; both fixed by the SAME pre-aggregate edit. For gap-day correctness: use RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '6' DAY PRECEDING on the daily CTE OR LEFT JOIN a date spine + COALESCE missing days to 0 + then ROWS frame.
• Rolling/cumulative-distinct HLL — Trino 467: COUNT(DISTINCT col) OVER (...) is NOT supported (trinodb/trino #7885); same for approx_distinct(col) OVER (...) (approx_distinct is not a window function). For rolling N-day distinct user count per day, two patterns: (PRIMARY, ~2.3% error, cheap) build a daily HLL sketch table `CREATE TABLE daily_user_hll AS SELECT event_date, CAST(approx_set(user_id) AS varbinary) AS user_id_hll FROM events GROUP BY event_date` THEN self-join `cardinality(merge(CAST(s2.user_id_hll AS HyperLogLog)))` over a trailing INTERVAL range grouped by s1.event_date; (SECONDARY, exact, expensive) self-join raw events over trailing INTERVAL window grouped by window_end_day with plain COUNT(DISTINCT) — this is allowed because the outer aggregate is a plain GROUP BY aggregate, not a window function. The CAST(... AS HyperLogLog) is mandatory when reading from the stored varbinary column. `approx_set` precision is FIXED at ~2.3% (no `approx_set(x, e)` overload); the scalar `approx_distinct(x, e)` takes the optional precision arg with valid range [0.0040625, 0.26000].
• Long-to-wide pivot (conditional aggregation) — Trino 467: NO `PIVOT` keyword exists. Write conditional aggregation manually with one of three equivalent forms: (IDIOMATIC TRINO) `count_if(status='pending')` for count-where-true; (ANSI-standard) `COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status='pending')` — supported on every Trino aggregate; (PORTABLE fallback) `SUM(CASE WHEN status='pending' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)` — works on every SQL engine. All three produce identical row counts and identical query plans on Trino 467. For SUM-of-metric per status: `SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE status='pending') AS pending_amount` is the FILTER form, `SUM(CASE WHEN status='pending' THEN amount END) AS pending_amount` is the CASE form (CASE returns metric on match, NULL otherwise; SUM ignores NULL so each output column collapses to the metric for the matching status). All three are zero-group-safe with GROUP BY entity — every entity appears in the output, including those with zero matching rows.
• NULL-handling in aggregates — Trino 467 (verbatim aggregate-page rule): COUNT(*) returns the number of input rows (NEVER skips NULL — counts every row including NULL-padded LEFT JOIN rows); COUNT(col) returns the number of non-null input values (skips NULLs in col). The exception list: `count()`, `count_if()`, `max_by()`, `min_by()`, `approx_distinct()` — these return 0 (not NULL) for zero non-null values OR for no input rows. All OTHER aggregates (SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, array_agg, listagg, bool_or, bool_and, arbitrary, approx_percentile, etc.) IGNORE NULL values and return NULL for no input rows OR when all values are NULL. AVG ignores NULL — denominator = count of non-NULL values, NOT count of all rows (i.e., AVG does NOT treat NULL as 0; a NULL row is excluded from BOTH numerator and denominator). SUM ignores NULL — sum of non-NULL values, NULL if no non-NULL values exist. COUNT(*) vs COUNT(col) split: COUNT(*) inflates by 1 per zero-match LEFT JOIN parent (counts the NULL-padded row), COUNT(right.key) yields 0 correctly. `COALESCE(COUNT(*), 0)` is vacuous because COUNT(*) never returns NULL — the fix is COUNT(right.key) not COALESCE.
